quoted_clause: The architecture is memory- and compute-sane at the 10 rps design point ... the ~18.6× prefill oversubscription at the 40 rps peak (40 × 1.29 ≈ 51.6 PFLOP/s vs the ~2.77 PFLOP/s host capacity)
observed: The 18.6× figure is demand versus ONE 8×H100 host's sustained prefill capacity, not versus the deployed fleet. At 10 rps the same arithmetic gives 10 × 1.29 = 12.9 PFLOP/s, which is already 4.66× one host's 2.77 PFLOP/s. If the 10 rps design point uses H hosts, the 40 rps fleet oversubscription is 51.6/(H × 2.77), not 18.6× unless H = 1. The mini-case therefore mixes per-host capacity with fleet-level oversubscription and contradicts its own 'compute-sane at 10 rps' claim.
correction: State the number of hosts at the 10 rps design point. Compute required host-equivalents at 10 rps (4.7) and 40 rps (18.6), and report fleet oversubscription as 18.6/H. Alternatively, explicitly say '18.6 host-equivalents of prefill capacity' rather than '18.6× oversubscription'.
acceptance_test: Recompute the mini-case with an explicit H. Show that 10 rps demand is 12.9 PFLOP/s, 40 rps demand is 51.6 PFLOP/s, and the fleet oversubscription at peak is 51.6/(H × 2.77). The text must not call 18.6× a fleet oversubscription unless H = 1.
verdict_evidence: chapter-06.md:131 'compute-sane at 10 rps ... ~18.6x ... vs ~2.77 PFLOP/s host capacity'; 10 rps = 12.9 PFLOP/s = 4.66x one host; :91 reads same number as 19 host-equivalents.
fix_instruction: Name the denominator - '18.6x one host's prefill capacity (18.6 host-equivalents)' - and state the deployed host count.

page_hint: Ch 6 'Reading Telemetry Into a Decision' and §8 mini-case
quoted_clause: KV cache hit ratio low (resource: memory) ... KV cache occupancy at 85% with low prefix-hit ratio (resource, memory/FLOP pressure)
observed: The text conflates two different quantities: KV-cache occupancy (a memory-capacity signal) and prefix-cache hit ratio (a reuse/compute signal). A low prefix-cache hit ratio means more prefill recomputation; it is not itself evidence of memory pressure. Conversely, high KV occupancy is a memory signal even when prefix hits are high. Labeling 'KV cache hit ratio low' as 'resource: memory' misclassifies the bottleneck.
correction: Separate the dashboard signals: 'KV-cache occupancy' → memory capacity; 'prefix-cache hit ratio' → reuse/compute. In the mini-case, say 'KV occupancy 85% (memory pressure) and low prefix-hit ratio (prefill recomputation)' rather than grouping both under memory.
acceptance_test: A dashboard with high KV occupancy and high prefix-hit ratio must be distinguishable from one with high occupancy and low prefix-hit ratio. The text must assign the correct resource layer to each.
verdict_evidence: ch06 L91 tags 'KV cache hit ratio low (resource: memory)' but paragraph reads it as prefill compute; L118 treats prefix caching as prefill-work reduction.
fix_instruction: L91: label 'KV cache hit ratio low' as resource: FLOP/reuse (prefill recomputation); keep KV occupancy 85% (L131) as the memory signal.

correction: Replace 'zeroing goodput' with 'can reduce goodput' or 'can erase the throughput gain'.
acceptance_test: The Common Mistakes bullet must be consistent with Scenario B: a p95 breach can coexist with higher goodput.
verdict_evidence: ch06 L108 'zeroing goodput' contradicts L62 Scenario B where p95 breach at 94% compliance raises goodput 48 -> 65.8.
fix_instruction: Replace 'zeroing goodput' with 'can erase the throughput gain' (or 'can reduce goodput').

quoted_clause: §1: "These are the dependent variables; they are what the SLO is written against — the canonical SLO targets are TTFT 1.2 s / TPOT ~25 ms." | §4: "State the SLO window (p95 ≤ 2 s TTFT) before quoting any rate" | Ch 5: "TTFT budget 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill), TPOT ~25 ms/token; p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s, p95 TPOT ≤ 35 ms."

page_hint: Ch 6 §3, 'Apply this to the canonical workload'; compare Ch 6 §3 'Reading Telemetry Into a Decision' and Ch 6 §8
quoted_clause: "Suppose a flash crowd (the ~40 rps peak) causes prefill requests to queue. If on average the batch is well-behaved, p50 TTFT might sit at ~1.0 s. But the jobs that arrive behind ~1–2 same-time prefill requests each pay the full 1.08 s prefill of the job(s) ahead of them, so p95 TTFT drifts to ~2.5 s."
observed: The queueing model assumes only one or two prefill jobs ahead of an arriving request. The same chapter, two paragraphs later, computes that at the 40 rps peak the host is ~18.6× oversubscribed on prefill (51.6 PFLOP/s demand vs 2.77 PFLOP/s sustained), which means the queue is unbounded, not one-to-two deep, and that p95 TTFT would drift far past 2.5 s. The two passages describe incompatible operating regimes for the same event (the 40 rps peak).
correction: State the fleet assumption explicitly in the example and reconcile it: either (a) note that the 1–2-jobs-ahead model describes a fleet sized for the peak (≈19–22 hosts, Ch 8 §3) rather than one host, or (b) replace the example with the single-host behaviour the chapter actually derives (queue growth at 18.6× oversubscription, p95 TTFT unbounded until admission control), and keep the 2.5 s figure only as the multi-host case.
acceptance_test: Every queueing illustration in Ch 6 states the fleet size it assumes, and the single-host and fleet-wide behaviours are not conflated.
verdict_evidence: ch6:56 derives p95 2.5 s from '~1-2 same-time prefill requests' at 40 rps peak; ch6:91 puts same peak at 18.6x oversubscribed with queue growth — ~43 in-flight prefills per host, not 1-2.
fix_instruction: ch06:56: state the fleet assumed, or replace with the 18.6x single-host queue growth and keep 2.5 s only as the ~19-22-host case (ch08:174).
